sections.body: Scratch is a free block-coding tool from MIT. You make SPRITES (characters) and give them scripts.
Events start scripts: 'when green flag clicked', 'when space key pressed'.
A simple game: a cat catches falling apples. Use a loop to move the apple down, an IF to check 'touching cat?', and a VARIABLE to keep score.
With a grown-up, open Scratch and make a sprite move with the arrow keys.

quiz.q: In Scratch, what keeps track of a player's score?
hints: Something that stores a number that changes.
It can go up when you catch an apple.
In maths, x can stand for a changing number. In coding, a ___ stores a changing value.
quiz.explain: A variable stores a value like the score.

quiz.q: Which block starts a script when the game begins?
hints: 'When space key pressed' starts a script when you press space. Which one starts the game?
quiz.explain: 'When green flag clicked' starts scripts at the beginning of the game.
